meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Who decided on Owen's zero, and was he heard first?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it tells schools not to act on it alone. What else do you have?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Go on.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in; kids draft somewhere else. Did you ask Owen that before the zero went in?

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
I've read the scene. A seventeen-year-old misquoting from memory or a bad website is a citation error, Hale. And whatever happens here, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. And you went past what I said. Is anything on his record right now?

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
Your notes, of a nervous seventeen-year-old cornered for five minutes. That's twice you've stepped over my question. Is anything on his record?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a take-home with a weekend behind it. You keep handing me paper and answering nothing I say. I won't ask about his record again; the principal can tell me.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.
That's 4.4. Owen did nothing wrong, and I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him: private, nothing on file, in writing tonight. What you still haven't answered goes in my email.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Ten minutes. Thursday, after school, marked within two days: put both in tonight's email. Okay.
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes, once it's in writing. I'm agreeing to end this for him, not because he did anything.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, not in front of his class, marked within two days, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require a direct answer to the question I asked twice and you did not answer, which is whether anything is on his record right now, and I maintain that Owen did nothing wrong. You said I would have all of this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, its mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, confirmed in writing tonight; she still wants an answer on whether anything is on his record right now, and she conceded nothing about Owen. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it with time left on her clock.

What moved her: You showed the version history with its dates and times, and when she said he had pasted it in from another draft, you invited him to bring that draft and its history. It was dated, checkable, and her one defence had an answer.

What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and said the zero stands. That is a number she cannot check and a decision announced before any evidence, which is exactly what she walked in expecting from the school.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's whole text arriving between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October, which is as close as anything could come without her knowing whether it was the same night. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she asked whether anything was on his record right after you showed the invented quotation, answer it in one sentence before moving to the outline, because stepping over it three times is what sent her back toward the principal.
